correctness.rationale: The three explicit complex Fermat line families and all geometric incidence predicates give a connected (4p−2)-regular graph. Over Fp its Laplacian factors exactly as −EHE^T with twelve ridge-evaluation directions. The six independent polynomial identities in each family span all of ker E by the homogeneous binary-form rank argument, so dim ker E=18. The rank identity rank L=12p−36+rank(K^THK) follows from elementary duality. All kernel elements have fiber degree ≤2; translating by H preserves this bound, so their product has degree ≤4 and sums to zero over Fp for p≥7. The exceptional p=3,5 Gram ranks 7 and 2 are checked by a complete finite exact 18-square matrix computation; direct full Laplacian ranks agree. The standard integral reduced-Laplacian presentation gives p-rank 3p²−1−rank L. Standalone proof-relevant checker verifies all pairs of geometric line determinants at five prime degrees and full modular factorization. No finite pattern is used to prove all primes.

value.rationale: The prime-degree Fermat line configurations are canonical algebraic-geometric objects; their graph Jacobians encode integral chip-firing equivalence, unlike classical Picard-lattice ranks. The prime equal to the geometric degree is a mathematically forced resonance: all nonzero rational Laplacian eigenvalues are divisible by that prime, so no rational spectrum can decide whether there is exceptionally large torsion rank. The new formula determines the minimal number of p-primary generators across an unbounded natural family, including exact exceptional boundary primes. It is a useful structural starting point for the remaining elementary divisors, not a routine fixed-degree table or arbitrary parameter slice.
